doc.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011

title: Son Ricky's early drumming
summary: His son played drums as an infant and as a toddler surprised Sal Nistico by sitting in.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Anyway, it’s pretty cool how your son [Rick Montalbano Jr.] has found his way into music. And I bet he was a drummer from an early age.

Yes, from — he was sitting at the drums from when he was an infant he would be on my lap or Jill’s lap, and it was one of the ways — he was a very loud, hyper kid and one of the ways we would calm him down is to put on music and sit him on our lap and put the sticks in his hands and he would just start — and pretty soon it was obvious that he was actually playing the songs. He was playing the melody on the drums you know. So yeah, he showed signs of getting it from very early on. I could never quite get him to go to the piano the way he should have because he could have really been a good piano player. But a little bit of the father-son thing with the piano. But see I didn’t play the drums that well. I only played the drums for amusement. So I think he figured out right away that he could beat me at that. Yeah I can remember Sal Nistico in our music room at home, staying at my house and we were in there playing and Ricky just snuck in and he was just a little, I don’t know, three years old or four years old or something. He came in and we were working out some tunes and he sat down at the drums and started playing. And Sal just was playing like he didn’t realize what was going on at first. Then he happened to look © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -18-

over and he did a double take, like what the heck is that, you know, your kid’s playing the drums and we’re playing. We were playing. We weren’t like playing to make him sound good, he was playing with us and it was working. And when he looked over at Ricky, Ricky stuck his tongue out at him. And for days afterwards he would just say “man, what’s with your kid?”
